onboarding.body: Groups only change where sessions appear; they never move sessions or logs. Drag sessions into groups, and drag group headers to reorder or nest them.

config.details.diagnostics:
What it does: shows the drag-target HUD and writes group operations, drags, renders, and revisions to a local NDJSON trace.
When to enable: only temporarily when diagnosing drag targets, anchors, virtualization, or layout. Keep it off for normal use.
Security: the trace lives in the local DSH storages directory and may contain group IDs, session IDs, paths, viewport sizes, and operation sequences. Session message text is not recorded by default, but other local programs may read the file.
Other impact: small memory, CPU, and disk writes. Disabling stops new writes but does not delete existing trace files.
config.details.debugProbe:
What it does: enables the local .debug.ndjson probe and records dialog sizes, positions, and layout calculations.
When to enable: only in development or while reproducing dialog geometry, drag, or resize bugs. Leave it off in production.
Security: exposes a local debugging endpoint and layout data that may contain session/group IDs and window dimensions. Do not leave it on in an untrusted environment.
Other impact: extra debug-file writes and requests. Disabling turns the endpoint off.
config.details.controlApi:
What it does: enables the native session_groups_control tool and retains the browser/debug HTTP control routes for reading group state, planning, and applying group changes.
When to enable: only when you want AI or trusted local automation to manage groups. Keep it off for ordinary manual use.
Security: callers can enumerate and change groups and session ownership. Prompt injection or a compromised local process could make unintended changes. The native tool runs in-process and does not cross the browser fence; HTTP routes remain behind the browser-session fence. Only allow trusted AI/local callers.
Other impact: creates and maintains a local control token and registers the native tool. Disabling makes the tool and routes refuse operations immediately, but does not roll back existing group data.
config.details.controlDestructive:
What it does: allows the AI control surface to delete groups. Deleting a non-empty group requires moving its sessions and child groups to a destination; it never deletes or archives the sessions themselves.
When to enable: only temporarily when you explicitly want AI to delete a group. Keep it off for normal use.
Security: this is a high-privilege operation. A mistaken call can permanently remove a group hierarchy and change session ownership. Confirm the target and destination, and keep a backup of the group file.
Other impact: the UI does not undo deletion; recovery generally requires rebuilding from a dsh-session-groups.json backup. Do not treat this as an everyday setting.
config.details.controlSessions:
What it does: lets AI/tools inspect session titles, rename sessions, and archive or restore sessions.
When to enable: only when you want AI to manage session titles or archived state. Keep it off when managing groups only.
Security: renaming changes how a session appears in lists; archiving a running session may stop active work (requiring explicit stopActivity). Archiving is reversible, but an incorrect rename or archive can affect recognition and visibility. Always use an explicit sessionId; never guess.
Other impact: titles and archive state belong to DSH core session state, not the group document, so they cannot form one transaction with a group move.
